canonical_definition: MT-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating instruction-following capabilities in single-turn and multi-turn dialogue settings, using LLM-as-a-judge methodologies (primarily GPT-4, sometimes GPT-3.5) to assess open-ended dialogue quality, complex cognitive tasks (e.g., mathematics, reasoning, writing), and roleplay performance. It involves models responding to diverse prompts with quality judgments aggregated across multiple interactions, often emphasizing task-aware parameter efficiency, safety alignment, or instruction tuning effectiveness. Some papers frame it specifically as measuring multi-turn interaction quality, while others highlight its role in assessing general assistant capabilities or specialized domains like biomedicine.
